title: Snippet test runner (CI) — design notes (mock + optional staging)
content:
Context / why we’re doing this
- We keep getting drift between:
  - docs-site snippets
  - SDK README snippets
  - redwood-examples canonical snippets
- Recent gateway + SDK changes made drift more painful (stream event shapes, tool_call arg deltas, structured output schema mode).
- Goal is NOT to build a heavy E2E suite; we want a lightweight harness that makes it hard to merge obviously broken snippets.

Non-goals (explicit)
- Validate model quality / exact token outputs.
- Benchmark latency/throughput.
- Enforce a single SDK API surface (we can only test what each SDK supports).

High-level approach
- Treat snippets as small programs with a standard header + minimal configuration.
- Run them in CI under two modes:
  1) Mock mode (default, always-on): deterministic mock server that emulates Redwood API behavior enough to exercise parsing/loops.
  2) Staging mode (optional, gated): run a small subset against a real staging endpoint to catch integration mismatches.
- Primary enforcement: “snippet compiles + runs + asserts expected event semantics and final object shape.”

What counts as a snippet for CI
- Canonical location: redwood-examples repo holds the source-of-truth.
- Docs + SDK READMEs should link to canonical snippets, or import them via tooling where feasible.
- Snippet granularity:
  - streaming-basic (token deltas + final response)
  - tools-single (tool_call delta accumulation + invocation + follow-up completion)
  - tools-parallel (multiple tool calls in a single turn, with concurrency control)
  - structured-output (schema + validate + retry-on-parse-failure)

Repository layout (proposed)
- redwood-examples/
  - python/
    - streaming_basic.py
    - tools_single.py
    - tools_parallel.py
    - structured_output.py
  - typescript/
    - streaming-basic.ts
    - tools-single.ts
    - tools-parallel.ts
    - structured-output.ts
  - go/
    - streaming_basic/
    - tools_single/
    - tools_parallel/
    - structured_output/
  - internal/
    - mock-server/
    - runner/

Runner design sketch
- Single entrypoint: `./ci/run-snippets` (thin wrapper around a language-agnostic runner)
- Runner responsibilities:
  - enumerate snippets (language + name + mode requirements)
  - start mock server (if needed)
  - inject env vars (REDWOOD_BASE_URL, REDWOOD_API_KEY, etc.)
  - run snippets with timeouts and capture stdout/stderr
  - enforce “no secrets printed” heuristics (see below)
  - produce JUnit-style output for CI UI (optional but nice)

Why not just run everything against staging?
- Rate limits / cost + intermittent staging instability would create noisy failures.
- Some snippets (streaming) are sensitive to proxies/timeouts; staging failures are hard to triage.
- Mock mode catches 80% of the bugs (broken loops, incorrect event handling, JSON parsing errors) deterministically.

Mock server approach
- Provide a small HTTP server that implements a subset of the Redwood API used by snippets.
- Must support:
  - non-streaming completion response
  - streaming responses with event sequences for:
    - content/token deltas
    - tool_call deltas (partial JSON arguments across multiple frames)
    - final response / terminal event
  - structured output response with a schema-ish payload (and ability to simulate malformed output)

Event semantics to emulate (note to self: align w/ canonical patterns doc)
- Streaming: emit a sequence that forces clients to do the “right thing”:
  - at least 2 content delta events
  - at least 2 tool_call argument delta events when tools enabled
  - final event containing a complete message + tool calls (or final response object)
- Tool calling: include a realistic partial JSON args sequence, e.g. "{\"city\": \"San" then " Francisco\"}".
- Structured output: provide two fixtures:
  - valid JSON matching schema
  - invalid JSON (e.g., trailing comma or wrong field type) so the retry flow is exercised

Mock fidelity choices (trade-offs)
- Keep response shapes limited to what snippets need.
- Avoid “accidentally” teaching clients to rely on mock-only fields.
- Where possible, reuse OpenAPI schema fragments, but don’t block on it.
- Determinism is more important than full API coverage.

How snippets should assert correctness (lightweight)
- Streaming basic:
  - assert we observed at least one content delta
  - assert final aggregated text contains an expected substring (fixture-driven)
  - assert we received a final/terminal event
- Tools:
  - assert tool_call id/name is stable across deltas
  - assert args JSON parses ONLY after aggregation
  - assert tool dispatch uses allowlist and fails closed on unknown tool
  - assert follow-up call includes tool result and produces final assistant message
- Structured output:
  - validate decoded object against schema (Zod in TS, jsonschema/Pydantic in Python, gojsonschema or custom validator in Go)
  - if first decode fails, retry once with a stricter instruction (fixture ensures second pass succeeds)

Staging gating plan
- Two tiers:
  - Tier A (always): mock mode on every PR.
  - Tier B (gated): staging mode only on:
    - nightly schedule
    - manual workflow_dispatch
    - release branches / tagged releases
- Staging config:
  - require REDWOOD_STAGING_API_KEY in CI secrets
  - run a reduced set (maybe 1 per category per language) to keep runtime/cost low
  - enforce strict per-snippet timeout (e.g., 60s) and global budget

CI integration points
- Primary: redwood-examples repo CI runs full suite (mock mode) per PR.
- Secondary (optional): SDK repos + docs repo run a smaller “link check + smoke” job:
  - verify README/docs code blocks link to canonical snippet paths + commit hash
  - optionally run only language-relevant snippets (e.g., python-only in python SDK repo)

Docs-site snippet verification (open question)
- Option 1: docs site only links to examples, no code blocks maintained directly.
- Option 2: docs keep code blocks, but we generate them from canonical snippets at build time.
- Leaning Option 2 if tooling is straightforward; otherwise keep it simple and link.

Secrets handling + redaction
- In mock mode, no API key required; runner sets REDWOOD_API_KEY="mock".
- In staging mode:
  - ensure snippets never print env vars
  - runner should scan stdout/stderr for common secret patterns:
    - presence of the literal key value (we can pass it as masked secret and still be cautious)
    - lines containing "REDWOOD_API_KEY" / "Authorization:" etc.
  - fail the job if suspicious output detected

Rate-limit + safety defaults
- Mock mode should not do sleeps > minimal.
- Staging mode:
  - concurrency = 1 (or very small) to avoid bursts
  - tokens requested should be tiny
  - use a fixed small model (or staging-only model alias) to stabilize behavior

Timeouts + flake control
- Every snippet run should have:
  - per-snippet timeout
  - cancellation support (AbortController in TS, context in Go, signal/timeout in Python)
- Streaming tests should tolerate small timing differences but must not hang.
- If staging streaming flakes are too high, we limit staging to non-streaming structured output + tool-call (non-stream) until stability improves.

Maintenance expectations (be honest)
- Someone will need to update mock fixtures when:
  - gateway event names change
  - SDK changes iteration API or response types
  - we add a new canonical example category
- Estimate: 0.5–1 day/month once stable; spikes during major API changes.
- Proposed owner rotation: CI harness owned by DevEx (me), with per-language owners keeping their snippets compiling.

Open questions / TODO
- Do we want the mock server to live in:
  - redwood-examples (simpler)
  - a shared internal repo (more reuse)
- Go validator choice for structured output: gojsonschema vs manual + tests.
- Exact contract for “final event”: some SDKs expose `finalResponse()` / `response` after stream ends; ensure consistent example narrative.
- Need decision from Marcus (security): is it acceptable to include a toy tool that reads local files? My vote: NO; keep tools to pure functions with hardcoded outputs.

Proposed next steps (week 1)
- Lock minimal event fixtures with Ibrahim (align with canonical patterns doc).
- Implement mock server with 4 routes corresponding to the 4 snippet categories.
- Implement runner script + CI job in redwood-examples.
- Add docs + SDK repo checks: link validation to canonical paths.

Notes from discussions (quick captures)
- Dana: TS streaming examples must use AbortSignal; runner should enforce an upper bound so we don’t hang in CI.
- Mateusz: Go examples should use context.WithTimeout by default; avoid bufio.Scanner default token limit issues.
- Elliot: docs needs a stable permalink strategy; if we link to canonical examples, use versioned links (tagged release or commit hash) to avoid docs pointing at main.
- Connor: for release, we should run staging tier as part of go/no-go checklist (not necessarily on every PR).
